item.title: Too Hot
item.description:
It has been too hot to do anything today.

I opened the window, closed the curtains and put a fan beside the desk, which just moved the warm air around faster.

At one point the computer sounded louder than usual. I put my hand near it and decided it was probably fine.

People worry too much about temperatures. Machines are designed to get hot. That’s why they have fans.

I was going to spend the afternoon sorting out some files, but instead I lay on the floor for a while because it was colder there. Ended up watching videos on my phone until the battery warning came on.

item.title: The Leak
item.description:
Had a serious leak tonight.

Tea went all over my desk.

Luckily most of it missed the keyboard, although a notebook took a direct hit and now several pages of operational notes are permanently brown.

This is why I never keep everything digital. You can’t hack paper. You can spill tea on it, apparently, but that’s a separate threat model.

I spent twenty minutes moving cables and wiping everything down. The computer stayed on through the whole incident, which proves the setup is more resilient than most corporate networks.

item.title: Delayed
item.description:
My train was delayed this morning.

First it was ten minutes, then twenty, then the board just said delayed as if time had stopped being relevant.

I got a coffee and sat near the window. There were about thirty other people staring at the same board like one of us might intimidate it into changing.

I could probably have changed it.

Those display systems are never as secure as people think. I didn’t touch it because changing the board wouldn’t make the train arrive any faster, and I don’t waste capabilities just to show off.

item.title: April Warning
item.description:
I don’t really like April Fools’ Day.

Most of the jokes are obvious and the rest are companies pretending they’ve invented a product nobody asked for.

This morning somebody posted that ZeroDays had finally recruited a real hacker.

I nearly believed it for a second.

Fair play, that was a good one.

Apparently a few of their members didn’t find it funny. One of them sent me a message saying I should be careful what I say about people online.

item.title: Wrong Number
item.description:
Got a message from a number I didn’t recognise tonight.

It just said, “Are you still coming tomorrow?”

I replied that they had the wrong number. That should have been the end of it, but they sent back, “Who is this then?”

Bad question.

I told them they had contacted a secure private line and that I was already running a trace. There was a long pause, then three messages arrived at once asking me not to hack them.

item.title: Frozen Morning
item.description:
It was freezing this morning.

I found this out after leaving the house in a hoodie because the sky looked bright through the window. That was a mistake.

The path was covered in ice and I nearly went straight over before I’d even closed the door. Managed to stay up, but only because I grabbed the wall in a way that probably looked very calm from a distance.

Got the bus into town and spent the whole journey trying to warm my hands up. The person behind me was watching videos without headphones, which should honestly be illegal before nine in the morning.

item.title: December Lights
item.description:
Put the Christmas lights up today.

I say “put them up” like it was a simple job. It took nearly two hours because they were tangled into a shape that shouldn’t be possible in normal space.

Every year I put them away properly. Every year they come back like this.

I’m not ruling out interference.

Once they were finally working, one section started blinking at a different speed from the rest. My first thought was that somebody was trying to send a message through them.

item.title: The Halloween Incident
item.description:
I wasn’t planning on doing anything for Halloween this year.

A few people asked if I wanted to go out, but it was raining and I had already bought a bag of sweets that was supposed to be for people calling to the door.

Hard to compete with that.

I watched half of a horror film, answered the door four times and then got dragged into an argument online because somebody said ZeroDays were the best hackers in Ireland.

item.title: ZeroDays Again
item.description:
I’ve seen people talking about ZeroDays again.

I genuinely don’t understand why people take those guys so seriously.

They’re skids.

That’s it.

I’ve watched people in that group spend hours talking themselves up over things that wouldn’t impress anyone who actually knew what they were doing. They seem to think using dramatic usernames and posting screenshots makes them some kind of elite group.

It doesn’t.

I normally wouldn’t bother mentioning them, but someone sent me a message asking if I was worried because apparently ZeroDays had been “looking into me”.

item.title: Summer Job
item.description:
I’ve been working a lot more recently, which is probably why I haven’t written anything for a while.

It’s not a particularly interesting job. Mostly the usual stuff, getting up too early, dealing with people who don’t know what they want, then coming home exhausted and pretending I’m going to do something productive.

I usually don’t.

The annoying thing is that I’ve actually got quite a lot of things I want to work on. I’ve got ideas for a few computer projects, a couple of games I’ve never finished and about ten films sitting on a list that I keep saying I’ll watch.

item.title: New Keyboard
item.description:
Finally replaced my keyboard today.

The old one was getting ridiculous. Half the keys needed to be hit twice and the space bar had developed this horrible squeak that made it sound like I was typing inside an old cupboard.

The new one is much quieter, which is nice because I tend to use my computer late at night.

Spent most of the afternoon setting everything up and moving things around on my desk. I also found a pile of receipts underneath my monitor that I have apparently been ignoring for several months.

item.title: The Guy Who Kept Arguing
item.description:
Some people genuinely don’t know when to stop talking.

I was in a group chat tonight and one guy kept arguing with everyone about absolutely everything. Nothing serious. Just one of those people who has to correct every sentence somebody writes.

Eventually he started having a go at me specifically.

I told him to leave it.

He didn’t.

Then he started with the usual stuff about how nobody could possibly know who he was because he didn’t use his real name.

item.title: Rainy Sunday
item.description:
It has rained pretty much all day.

I had planned to go out this morning but when I opened the curtains it looked like the entire street had been abandoned, so I went back to bed instead. Woke up again around eleven and spent another twenty minutes convincing myself that getting up was worth it.

Eventually I did.

Made some toast, cleaned the kitchen and then went into town to get a few things. I only needed shampoo and toothpaste but somehow came home with a new hoodie and a takeaway. This happens every time I go shopping.

item.title: Hello World
item.description:
Hello! Welcome to my blog.

I’ve been meaning to make one of these for ages but never really got around to it. Most of the stuff I do online ends up being random posts or messages that disappear after a few days, so I thought it would be nice to actually keep track of things somewhere.

I’ll probably write about whatever I’m doing, which could be anything from computers and random projects to films I’ve watched or places I’ve been.
